mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace an AMG GLA 45 engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: An AMG GLA 45 engine replacement typically costs between £3,800 and £12,000 depending on generation, condition type, and whether fitting is included. M133 units (X156, 2014-2020) range from £3,800 to £9,000, while M139 units (H247, 2020-present) range from £5,500 to £12,000. Rebuilt M133 (AMG GLA 45 X156): £3,800-£9,000 supply only. Rebuilt M139 (AMG GLA 45 / 45 S H247): £5,500-£12,000 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £2,800-£7,000 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £1,000-£2,000 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: Is the M133 engine in the AMG GLA 45 reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M133 is generally durable but can develop issues as mileage rises. It has several well-documented problems that owners should be aware of. Turbocharger failure due to oil feed line contamination. Timing chain stretch causing cold-start rattle. Oil leaks from valve cover gasket and oil filter housing. Carbon buildup on intake valves. Regular oil changes every 5,000-7,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M133 turbocharger failure in an AMG GLA 45?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M133's turbocharger typically shows warning signs before complete failure. Loss of power or reduced boost pressure. Whistling noise from the engine bay. Oil in the intake system. Excessive smoke from the exhaust. Check engine light illuminated with turbo-related fault codes.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the GLA 45 and GLA 45 S?

acceptedAnswer.text: The GLA 45 S is the higher-output variant of the second-generation H247 GLA 45, introduced in 2020 with the M139 engine. GLA 45 (standard): 382hp, 480Nm torque. GLA 45 S: 421hp, 500Nm torque. Both use the M139 2.0L turbo engine with different tuning. The S variant features a more aggressive exhaust and additional performance features.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my AMG GLA 45 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., turbocharger cartridge, timing chain tensioner, valve cover gasket). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic turbo failure. Turbocharger replacement at specialist: £1,500-£3,200 - do this at first sign of trouble. Timing chain tensioner replacement: £350-£600 - do this at first sign of rattle. Walnut blasting: £300-£500 - preventative every 50,000 miles. Full M133 rebuild: £4,500-£9,000 - for catastrophic failure or 100k+ miles. Full M139 rebuild: £5,500-£12,000 - for catastrophic failure or 80k+ miles. Given AMG GLA 45 values (£15,000-£60,000+), a rebuilt engine is typically excellent value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my AMG GLA 45 has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. AMG GLA 45 (X156, 2014-2020): M133.980 (2.0L turbo, 355-381hp). AMG GLA 45 (H247, 2020-present): M139.980 (2.0L turbo, 382hp). AMG GLA 45 S (H247, 2020-present): M139.980 (2.0L turbo, 421hp). Service history documents list engine type.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz AMG GLA 45 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes-AMG GLA 45 represents the pinnacle of compact SUV performance, powered by two generations of hand-built AMG four-cylinder engines - the M133 in the first-generation X156 (2014-2020) and the M139 in the second-generation H247 (2020-present). Both engines were, at their respective launches, the most powerful four-cylinder production engines in the world.

milestones.description: AMG GLA 45 launched with X156 generation, M133.980 2.0L turbo, 355hp (360 PS), 450Nm torque, 7-speed AMG SPEEDSHIFT DCT, 4MATIC AWD, 0-100km/h in 4.8 seconds
M133 upgraded to 381hp (280kW) and 475Nm torque via reconfigured valve assembly, timing and turbocharging
2019 - Service campaign initiated for turbocharger oil feed line contamination
All-new H247 GLA 45 launched with M139.980 2.0L turbo, 382hp (standard) and 421hp (S variant) - world's most powerful four-cylinder production engine
M139 introduced with 180-degree rotated layout, twin fuel injection, 9-speed AMG SPEEDSHIFT DCT, 4MATIC+ with drift mode

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz AMG GLA 45 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes-AMG GLA 45 is powered by two generations of hand-built AMG four-cylinder engines - the M133 and M139 - both remarkable engineering achievements that have developed well-documented reputations for specific, predictable failures. Turbocharger failure due to oil feed line contamination dominates M133 replacement demand, while M139 owners report cooling system strain and oil consumption concerns. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common AMG GLA 45 engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: M133 Turbocharger Failure - Why the AMG GLA 45 Loses Boost and Generates Smoke
problems.rootCause: The M133 engine runs up to 1.8 bar (26.1 psi) of boost, creating extreme heat in the turbocharger housing. Insufficient cool-down periods after hard driving can coke the oil feed lines, restricting oil flow to the turbo bearings. A Mercedes Service Campaign was initiated for GLA 45 turbocharger failure due to contamination of the oil feed line. The result is progressive bearing wear, shaft play, and eventual turbo failure with metallic debris entering the intercooler.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace turbo cartridge, clean oil feed lines, replace oil and filter
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-70k miles. Viable if caught early with no internal engine debris

repairOptions.tier: Major - Full Turbo Unit & Intercooler Flush
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Turbo replacement plus intercooler removal and chemical flush to remove metal debris
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-70k miles. Required if turbo bearings have failed and shed debris

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M133 with new turbocharger, upgraded oil feed lines, timing chain
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary when turbo debris has scored cylinder walls

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical AMG GLA 45 (X156) is worth £15,000-£30,000 depending on age, mileage and condition - the full replacement cost of £4,500-£9,000 is modest relative to vehicle value. For vehicles worth under £15,000, evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: On an AMG GLA 45, do not cut corners on turbo maintenance. If you hear whistling or notice oil consumption above 1 litre per 1,000 miles, have the turbo inspected immediately. A specialist turbo replacement is painful but far less painful than a full engine rebuild. Also, fit a turbo timer or religiously idle the engine for 60 seconds after hard driving - it doubles turbo bearing life on the M133.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M133 Mercedes Benz AMG GLA 45 engine prices

problems.h4: M133 / M139 Timing Chain Stretch - Why the AMG GLA 45 Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can lose oil pressure retention when parked, allowing chain slack and producing a rattling noise on cold start. If ignored, the chain can stretch beyond acceptable tolerances, causing timing drift and potentially leading to valve-to-piston contact. This affects both M133 and M139 engines.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioner, oil and filter change
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-60k miles. Only viable if no chain damage yet

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-100k miles. Corrects the root cause properly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M133 or M139 with new timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if chain has jumped

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On an AMG GLA 45 worth £15,000-£50,000+, the timing chain replacement at £1,500-£2,500 is a justifiable investment. Full engine replacement is only necessary for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: At the first sign of rattling on cold start, have the timing chain tensioner inspected immediately - ignoring it can lead to catastrophic engine failure. Mercedes timing chain problems typically manifest between 40,000 and 80,000 miles. On higher-mileage M133 and M139 engines, a full rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components eliminates this risk entirely.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M133 / M139 Mercedes Benz AMG GLA 45 engine prices

problems.h4: M133 Oil Leaks & Carbon Buildup - Why the AMG GLA 45 Loses Oil and Power
problems.rootCause: Oil leaks from the valve cover gasket and oil filter housing are common on higher-mileage M133 engines. Additionally, the direct-injection system causes carbon buildup on intake valves, leading to misfires, flat spots, and reduced performance.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket, breather seals
Walnut blast intake valves, clean throttle body, reset adaptations
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-80k miles. Recommended every 50,000 miles for DI engines

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M133 with new gaskets, decarbonised head
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. For catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On an AMG GLA 45 worth £15,000-£30,000, valve cover gasket replacement at £300-£500 and walnut blasting at £300-£500 are sensible maintenance items. Full engine replacement is only justified for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: The M133's carbon buildup is an inherent trait of direct-injection performance engines - budget for walnut blasting every 50,000 miles to maintain peak performance. Oil leaks from valve cover gaskets should be addressed promptly; oil dripping onto hot exhaust components can create smoke and, in extreme cases, fire risk.

problems.group: M139 Cooling System Strain & Oil Consumption
problems.h4: M139 Cooling System Strain & Oil Consumption - High-Performance AMG Engine Wear
problems.rootCause: The M139 produces up to 421hp from just 2.0 litres - extreme output that generates significant heat. The engine runs hot when pushed, with temperatures reaching 100-105°C under hard use. Some owners report higher-than-normal oil consumption, necessitating more frequent top-ups.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect cooling system, replace thermostat if required, pressure test
Replace radiator, expansion tank, flush heater core
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-80k miles. If cooling system degradation is present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M139 with upgraded cooling system components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required for catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical H247 AMG GLA 45 or 45 S is worth £35,000-£60,000+ - the full replacement cost of £5,500-£12,000 is modest relative to vehicle value. A rebuilt engine is excellent value for preservation.
problems.recommendation: The M139's extreme power output demands meticulous cooling system maintenance. If you notice the engine running consistently hot or oil consumption increasing, have the cooling system inspected immediately. The M139's high-output nature means it requires more frequent oil checks than standard engines - check oil levels every 1,000 miles and top up as needed.
